title: Depth-three lifting from a principal quotient
statement: Let A be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of depth at least three [def-weil-pbc-depth], let f belong to its maximal ideal, and let U be the complement of its closed point in Spec A [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Set i:Spec(A/(f)) → Spec A to be the quotient map and V=i⁻¹(U). Let q:Y → U be finite etale [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume the actual pullback Y ×_U V → V extends to a finite etale r₀:F₀ → Spec(A/(f)), with a specified isomorphism of its restriction to the pullback over V [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then q extends to a finite etale r:F → Spec A with an isomorphism Y ≅ r⁻¹(U) over U. No regularity, henselian assumption or nonzerodivisor assumption on f is imposed.

proof.text: Construct a compatible finite flat model with etale principal quotient by the completion, henselian lifting and finite gluing argument.

Apply the proved finite-local principal-quotient differential criterion to get formal unramifiedness of this model. Finiteness over the Noetherian base gives local finite presentation. Mathlib Etale.of_formallyUnramified_of_flat combines it with flatness; retain the model’s punctured isomorphism and its morphism equality.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_etale_extension_of_depth_three_of_quotient_extension (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] (f : A) (hf : f ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) (hdepth : (3 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := A) A) (U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens) (hU : ∀ x : Spec (.of A), x ∈ U ↔ x ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint A) {Y : Scheme.{u}} (q : Y ⟶ U.toScheme) [IsFinite q] [Etale q] (hquot : let i := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {f}))) let V := i ⁻¹ᵁ U ∃ (F₀ : Scheme.{u}) (r₀ : F₀ ⟶ Spec (.of (A ⧸ Ideal.span {f}))), IsFinite r₀ ∧ Etale r₀ ∧ ∃ e₀ : pullback q (i ∣_ U) ≅ (r₀ ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme, e₀.hom ≫ r₀ ∣_ V = pullback.snd q (i ∣_ U)) : ∃ (F : Scheme.{u}) (r : F ⟶ Spec (.of A)), IsFinite r ∧ Etale r ∧ ∃ e : Y ≅ (r ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme, e.hom ≫ r ∣_ U = q
